evidence.functional_evidence: sign_as_registrar and sign_as_dean accept any signer, so the multi-sig credential can be forged by an outsider. The core trust path is broken.

limitations: BUG: sign_as_registrar and sign_as_dean accept any signer. SignCredential has a signer but never compares it to a registrar, a dean or the university authority, so any wallet can supply either signature. The script shows an unrelated wallet R setting registrar_signed. One outsider can call both and make any unrevoked credential verify as valid.

BUG: SignCredential doesn't tie the credential to the university it passes (no has_one = university), and nothing stops the same wallet signing twice in both roles. The "multi-sig" is two flags anyone can set.

BUG: initialize_university stores the authority argument but seeds the PDA by the signer. If they differ, the account can never be used: issue_credential re-derives the PDA from the stored authority and fails ConstraintSeeds, as the script shows with X naming U. The app always passes the connected wallet, so it is only reachable from a script.
create_disclosure_proof takes any credential_key and never checks the credential exists or belongs to the signing student (code reading; the script only exercised a student's own credential).
Revocation needs the university authority (has_one), which the script confirms. Revoked credentials reject new signatures and verify as false.
One university per wallet, because the PDA is seeded only by the authority. Credential metadata is stored as plain text on chain; there is no privacy layer despite the "selective disclosure" naming.
